claims.text: The FeCoNiCrAl coating produced from 15–45 μm feedstock is too thin for the target application.
Changing the feedstock from 15–45 μm to 45–75 μm will increase deposition efficiency.
Changing the feedstock from 15–45 μm to 45–75 μm will produce a thicker FeCoNiCrAl bond coat.
The larger-particle coating will preserve coating integrity relative to the 15–45 μm baseline.
The larger-particle coating will maintain minimal as-sprayed oxidation.
Larger particles have a lower surface-area-to-volume ratio.
A lower particle surface-area-to-volume ratio reduces relative in-flight oxidation per unit mass.
Larger particles absorb and retain more thermal energy during flight.
Greater retained thermal energy in larger particles promotes better splat formation and layer build-up.
Increasing particle size increases the mass and momentum of in-flight particles.
The increased mass and momentum of larger particles cause them to form thicker splats.
Larger particles produce enhanced inter-particle bonding.
Improved deposition efficiency from larger particles reduces the need for multiple low-mass impacts and thereby increases coating thickness.
The particle-size intervention should remain effective in APS or HVOF when spray distance, gas flow, energy input, substrate preparation, and related parameters remain in optimized ranges.
Excessively large particles or an overly broad size distribution may compromise melting uniformity.
Excessively large particles or an overly broad size distribution may cause undesirable splashing or incorporation of unmelted particles.
The 15–45 μm baseline deposit undergoes moderate in-flight oxidation.
